purpose: Advance Candidate49 by proving that a completed workflow record cannot be replaced with a byte-identical different inode between its initial identity check and content read, and by binding JSON parsing plus the returned SHA-256 to one no-follow file descriptor.

byte_identical_inode_replacement.setup: Create a byte-identical unique regular replacement file, let the original deterministic record path pass its unique-file lstat check, and then atomically replace that path before the former path-based JSON read.
byte_identical_inode_replacement.former_behavior: The former validator opened the path again, read the byte-identical replacement inode, and returned completed_workflow_record_validated_no_provider_request.
byte_identical_inode_replacement.expected_final_error: Candidate49 workflow record file identity changed during read

implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.pre_open_identity: Require the deterministic path to be a link-count-one regular file under a real non-symbolic-link parent chain and retain its device and inode.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.open: Open the deterministic path read-only with O_CLOEXEC and O_NOFOLLOW when supported.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.opened_descriptor_gate: Immediately require fstat to report a link-count-one regular file with the exact pre-open device and inode.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.single_source_bytes_and_digest: Read all JSON bytes and calculate SHA-256 from the same open descriptor; no later path-based digest is allowed for the completed record.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.post_read_descriptor_gate: Require device, inode, link count, regular-file type, size, mtime_ns, and ctime_ns to remain unchanged across the descriptor read.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.post_parse_path_gate: After JSON decoding, revalidate the deterministic path as a unique regular file and require its device, inode, size, mtime_ns, and ctime_ns to equal the opened descriptor.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.reuse_paths: Plan inspection, pre-lock idempotent workflow reuse, within-lock idempotent reuse, and newly published record verification all return the descriptor-bound digest.
implemented_fd_pinned_read_contract.new_publication_verification: After durable atomic publication, reread the record through the same descriptor-bound contract and require the persisted JSON object to equal the object submitted to the writer.

decision.next_action: On or after 2026-07-27 16:30 Asia/Shanghai, run the fail-closed Candidate49 source-to-signal workflow. Any completed record reuse must pass descriptor-bound content and digest verification before it is treated as zero-request validated; then wait for lawful t+1 and t+3 daily evidence before paper settlement.
